title: hello-harness-designer — a harness that designs other harnesses (target: cli)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “A CrewHaus harness that designs OTHER CrewHaus harnesses by interviewing you about intent.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the designer interviews you on claude-fable-5.

beats.label: Name the two checkouts it reads
beats.cue: Its docs ladder tries $CWD first — and a starter directory is not the demos root. Name both paths and the “else git clone” branch never fires.

verify.note: step 2 of each resolution ladder in agent.instructions. Without it the designer falls to step 3 and clones demos + factory into ~/.crewhaus/*-cache on camera before it answers your first message. Must come after setup-env — demos/.env may carry an empty CREWHAUS_FACTORY_PATH — and the manifest's one persistent terminal carries the export into the Beat 3 run.

beats.label: Prove both resolve
beats.cue: The recipe index and the Zod schema the designer validates against — 582 lines and 3,162, both already on disk.

verify.note: both paths resolve from the starter dir, so the designer's step-1/step-2 ladder terminates before the clone branch

groups.title: Beat 1 · The designer, one block at a time

beats.label: The header: what it is, how to run it
beats.cue: “Reflexivity demonstrator” — a YAML spec that produces the harness that writes YAML.

beats.label: Name, shape, token budget
beats.cue: target: cli, max_tokens: 100000 — an interview plus a written spec is a long session.

beats.label: State the job
beats.cue: “Interview a user about their INTENT — not ask them which YAML fields to fill in.”

beats.label: Resolve the docs at startup
beats.cue: Recipes from demos, the Zod schema from factory — pulled to HEAD before it advises you.

beats.label: The interview method
beats.cue: One open question, walk the decision tree, at most four clarifiers, then read the recipe.

beats.label: Write a self-contained directory
beats.cue: No `../`, no absolute paths — anything outside the harness dir gets copied in first.

beats.label: Scaffold .env.example and README
beats.cue: The generated README runs from inside its own directory, never “from the repo root”.

beats.label: Compile before handing it back
beats.cue: “Never hand the user a spec you have not seen the compiler accept.”

beats.label: Offer to tune it against a dataset
beats.cue: If you have examples, it scaffolds an eval and runs crewhaus optimize --write-back.

beats.label: The never-ask rules
beats.cue: Never ask which tools, which mode, which shape — and never invent a target outside the 14.

beats.label: The rules that aren't negotiable
beats.cue: Anything with bash or network cites Recipe 41 and denies `rm -rf` and `sudo`.

beats.label: Six tools
beats.cue: read, write, edit, glob, grep, bash — enough to author a harness and compile it.

beats.label: Allow the reads and the five writes
beats.cue: mode: default, and the only pre-approved writes are the files a harness is made of.

beats.label: Fence the shell
beats.cue: A named allow-list, ask for every other Bash call, alwaysDeny on `rm -rf` and `sudo` — worth reading closely: a lone `*` never crosses a `/`, so `rm -rf live` hits the deny and `rm -rf /tmp/x` misses it and lands on the runtime's own ask gate instead.

beats.label: Hand compaction to Haiku
beats.cue: A long interview compacts — on a different model than the one doing the designing.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “lint: clean — no findings.” Parse, the IR passes, and the scope audit.

beats.label: Audit its own tool grants
beats.cue: The trick the designer plays on you, played on the designer: builtins ranked vs intent.

verify.note: keyword-ranks builtins against agent.instructions; flags implied-but-missing and possible over-grants

beats.label: Emit the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees.”

verify.note: 128 lines of IR — line 7 alone is the 8.5k-character instructions blob, so it goes to a file rather than scrolling the terminal

beats.label: Open the IR
beats.cue: Fold line 7 — the instructions arrive as one escaped 8.5k string — and what's left is the shape: the six tools, then every permission rule in the order the engine reads them.

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: Shape asserted, deps installed, booted to the credentials gate: GREEN with no key.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: Every permission rule you just typed, compiled into a program you own.

beats.label: Launch the designer
beats.cue: [needs-key] “agent ready” — then it waits at `you>`. You speak first; the docs resolution and the interview both happen on that first turn.

verify.note: interactive interview; needs Anthropic credentials. The REPL prints `agent ready (model: …). type "exit" to quit.` and prompts — the agent does not open the conversation

beats.label: Describe the intent
beats.cue: [needs-key] Straight from the spec's own header — plain English, no CrewHaus terms.
beats.text: I want an agent that watches USDC transfers and pings me on Telegram.

beats.label: Approve a gated Bash call
beats.cue: [needs-key] mode: default, and the allow-list patterns use a single `*` — so `git -C ../.. fetch`, `mkdir -p live/usdc-watcher` and the validation compile all fall through to `approve Bash … [y/N] >`. Fire this beat again each time one appears.

verify.note: reusable — click it from the beats panel whenever the REPL raises an approval prompt; a single `*` in a pattern compiles to [^/]*, so any argument containing a path separator misses its allow rule

beats.label: Answer the clarifiers
beats.cue: [needs-key] Each answer maps to a field: target, tools, permission rules, memory.
beats.text: Telegram only, and it should message me — it never writes files or moves funds.

beats.label: Tell it where to write
beats.cue: [needs-key] Point it at live/ so the take leaves no diff in the repo.
beats.text: Call it usdc-watcher and write it under live/.

beats.label: Decline the eval scaffold
beats.cue: [needs-key] The “if no” branch: which shape, why, and the exact commands to run it.
beats.text: No dataset yet — just give me the summary and the standalone commands.

beats.label: Exit
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell.

groups.title: One more thing · the harness it wrote

beats.label: Read the README it generated
beats.cue: [needs-key] cd in, compile, install, run — no repo root, no `../`, no sibling checkout.

verify.note: reads the README the interview writes; only exists after the Beat 3 run

beats.label: Put its spec through the same gate
beats.cue: [needs-key] The spec it wrote, checked the way you checked the designer's own.

verify.note: the generated spec only exists after the Beat 3 run; the compile itself needs no key
